## The one-line version

The lexical leg of hybrid search is PostgreSQL's **`ts_rank_cd`** — *cover density* ranking.
It was called `bm25` in the type system until P-013 renamed it. **It was never BM25, and the
two behave nothing alike.** If you are about to tune lexical relevance, tune the thing that
is actually running.

## What `ts_rank_cd` actually computes

Cover density scores **how tightly the query's lexemes cluster together** in the document —
a "cover" is a span containing all of them. That is a genuinely useful signal for a
multi-word phrase query. It has two properties that matter enormously here, and neither is
what "BM25" would lead you to expect:

**1. On a single-lexeme query it has nothing to measure.** There is no span between one
term and itself, so the score degenerates toward a function of raw occurrence, and huge
numbers of documents tie. Measured on this corpus (plan
`semantic-search-fingerprint-coverage-2026-08-03`): a single-lexeme query returning **913
matches produced 7 distinct scores.** A leg that emits 7 buckets for 913 rows contributes
almost no ordering information to the fusion — most of the "ranking" downstream of it is
tie-breaking by whatever comes next.

**2. There is no document-length normalization. At all.** `ts_rank_cd` takes an optional
integer `normalization` argument controlling length division; **omitted, it defaults to
`0` — no normalization.** Every call site in this repo omits it:

```ts
// packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/search/sources.ts — all legs, no 3rd argument
rank: sql`ts_rank_cd(${tsv}, q.andq)`,
rank: sql`ts_rank_cd(${tsv}, q.orq)`,
ts_rank_cd(body_tsv,    plainto_tsquery('english', ${query})) AS rank,
ts_rank_cd(content_tsv, plainto_tsquery('english', ${query})) AS rank,
```

BM25, by contrast, is *defined* by its length normalization (the `b` parameter) and its
saturating term-frequency (`k1`). Neither exists here. Calling this leg `bm25` did not
merely mislabel it — it implied a tuning surface that is not present.

## Why this matters: four fix directions died on it

A recall complaint ("theory" scoring 2/9 at recall@30) generated four independent fix
directions. **All four were measured and all four were dead**, and in hindsight every one
of them was refuted by the paragraph above:

| direction tried | measured outcome | why it was doomed |
|---|---|---|
| **Length normalisation** | on-topic turns average 2499 chars vs 2670 overall — no length skew to correct | there is no length term in the score to begin with |
| **A wider rerank pool** | 13.5s at 45ms/pair — cost-prohibitive | a wider pool re-ranks more *ties*; the input ordering carries no signal to widen |
| **Stage B re-rank** | recall 0.333 → 0.333, exactly unchanged | same reason — reordering a tied set |
| **Other built-in PG rankers** | `ts_rank_cd` is cover density; `ts_rank` differs but is still not BM25 | no built-in PG ranker implements BM25 |

The transferable point is not "these four ideas were bad." Each is a sensible thing to try
against a lexical ranker. **They were refuted by a property of the ranker that nobody had
read** — and the ranker's *name* actively pointed away from reading it. A day of measurement
substituted for ten minutes with the source.

## Reading a score: native vs fused

Two scores travel with a hit and they are **not comparable**:

- **`SearchHit.rankerScores`** — the *native* per-ranker score (P-001/WI-7505). A
  `ts_rank_cd` value is unbounded-positive and typically small; a cosine similarity is
  bounded `[-1, 1]`.
- **the fused RRF score** — reciprocal-rank fusion, whose value depends only on *rank
  position*, not on either native scale.

Comparing a fused score against a cosine threshold is meaningless, and it has produced a
confidently-wrong report here before: a post-fusion RRF score whose ceiling is ~`0.0328`
was read against a `0.45` cosine floor and reported as "99.9% of injections fall below the
floor." **A suspiciously round rate over thousands of samples is usually a definitional
artifact, not a finding.** `min-score.ts` documents the per-leg scales; read it before
setting any threshold.

## The naming, and why `bm25` still appears

P-013 renamed the leg `bm25` → `lexical` in `@papercusp/search`. **The string `bm25` is
still accepted as INPUT and that is deliberate — it is not a deprecation alias** (which
this repo otherwise bans). `provenance.ts` spells out why: a *host* may name its own
lexical source `bm25`, and such a source must still classify as lexical rather than be
silently dropped:

```ts
return ranker.startsWith('lexical') || ranker.startsWith('bm25');
```

So: `bm25` surviving in the predicate is a compatibility surface for foreign inputs, not a
leftover. Do not "finish the rename" by deleting it.

## What to do instead

- **Want real BM25?** It has to be built — no PostgreSQL built-in provides it. That is the
  one remaining live route for the recall complaint above (tracked as P-035, owner-gated).
- **Before tuning any ranker**, open the SQL and check (a) which ranking function, (b) its
  normalization argument, (c) whether the query is single- or multi-lexeme. Those three
  facts determine which tuning ideas are even coherent.
- **Never infer a ranker's behavior from its identifier.** This is the general form, and it
  cost four measured experiments: a name is documentation, and documentation drifts. The
  function call does not.
